settings.heroTitle: Collect Uzbekistan, one stamp at a time.
settings.heroLede: A pocket passport for the classic route: Tashkent, Samarkand, Bukhara and Khiva. Get an original stamp in every city and take the whole trip home in your pocket.
settings.rewardText: Collect all four stamps and show the full passport at the Khiva stamp point to claim your reward.

cities.name: Tashkent
cities.intro: The capital and your gateway. Most international flights land here, so this is where the route begins. Soviet-era boulevards, a metro that doubles as a gallery, and the busiest bazaar in the country.

places.title: Hazrati Imam complex
places.text: Old-city religious centre, home to one of the oldest surviving Qur'an manuscripts.

places.title: Chorsu Bazaar
places.text: Blue domed market. Come in the morning for bread, dried fruit and spices.

places.title: Tashkent Metro
places.text: Every station is decorated differently. Kosmonavtlar and Alisher Navoiy are the stand-outs.

places.title: Amir Timur Square
places.text: The modern centre of the city, next to the Hotel Uzbekistan and the Timurid Museum.

places.title: Minor Mosque
places.text: White marble mosque on the Ankhor canal, especially photogenic at sunset.

places.title: Museum of Applied Arts
places.text: A merchant's mansion filled with carved wood, ganch plaster and suzani embroidery.

food: Plov at lunchtime: it is traditionally served until early afternoon
Green tea everywhere, served in a piala bowl
cities.nextTravel: Afrosiyob high-speed train · about 2 h 15 min

cities.name: Samarkand
cities.intro: Timur's capital and the most famous view in Central Asia. Three madrasahs facing one square, turquoise domes and a necropolis of tiled mausoleums.

places.title: Registan
places.text: Three madrasahs around one square. Visit twice: in daylight and for the evening lights.

places.title: Gur-e-Amir
places.text: The mausoleum of Amir Timur, with a ribbed azure dome and gilded interior.

places.title: Shah-i-Zinda
places.text: An avenue of tiled tombs, the finest majolica in the country.

places.title: Bibi-Khanym Mosque
places.text: Once one of the largest mosques in the Islamic world.

places.title: Siyob Bazaar
places.text: Right next to Bibi-Khanym. Buy Samarkand non, the famous round bread.

places.title: Ulugh Beg Observatory
places.text: Remains of a 15th-century observatory and its giant meridian arc.

food: Samarkand plov, cooked with yellow carrots
Fresh Samarkand non straight from the bazaar
cities.nextTravel: Afrosiyob high-speed train · about 1 h 30 min

cities.name: Bukhara
cities.intro: A living old town where you walk everywhere. Trading domes, a 12th-century minaret and a citadel that ruled the emirate.

places.title: Poi Kalyan
places.text: The Kalyan Minaret and mosque, Bukhara's symbol since 1127.

places.title: Ark Fortress
places.text: The citadel of the Bukhara emirs, with museums inside its walls.

places.title: Lyabi-Hauz
places.text: A pool shaded by old mulberry trees. The evening meeting point of the old town.

places.title: Trading domes
places.text: Covered bazaars for jewellers, hat-makers and money-changers.

places.title: Samanid Mausoleum
places.text: A 10th-century brick masterpiece in a quiet park.

places.title: Chor Minor
places.text: A small gatehouse with four turquoise towers, hidden in the side streets.

food: Tea by Lyabi-Hauz in the evening
Halva and sweets from the trading domes
cities.nextTravel: Train or car · about 6–7 h. Start early in the morning.

cities.name: Khiva
cities.intro: The last stamp. Itchan Kala is a whole walled city of minarets, palaces and mosques, best explored on foot at sunrise and sunset.

places.title: Itchan Kala
places.text: The walled inner city, a UNESCO World Heritage site. One ticket covers most sights.

places.title: Kalta Minor
places.text: The unfinished turquoise minaret, Khiva's best-known landmark.

places.title: Islam Khoja Minaret
places.text: The tallest minaret in Khiva. Climb it for a view over the whole old town.

places.title: Kunya-Ark
places.text: The old fortress with a watchtower made for sunset photos.

places.title: Juma Mosque
places.text: A prayer hall supported by more than 200 carved wooden columns.

places.title: Tash-Hauli Palace
places.text: The khan's palace and harem, with some of the richest tilework in Khiva.

food: Shivit oshi: green dill noodles, a Khorezm speciality
Tea on a rooftop terrace at sunset

faq.a: No. It is a souvenir travel journal made to look like a passport. It is not an identity document.

faq.q: Do I have to follow the route in order?
faq.a: No. Start wherever your trip starts. The numbers are only the most common direction of travel.

faq.q: What if a stamp point is closed?
faq.a: Check the hours on the city page. If it is closed during the posted hours, message us and we'll find a solution.

faq.q: Can I get a stamp without visiting the city?
faq.a: No. Stamps are given only in person at official stamp points.

faq.q: How do I claim the reward?
faq.a: Show your passport with all four stamps at the final stamp point in Khiva.

faq.q: Is the site available in other languages?
faq.a: Russian and Uzbek versions are coming soon.
